clue.text: Hold back others going on the water

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece going on another sits on top of it, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: the rest means the others, everyone remaining
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep the others back as they set off by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the water' reads as boating, but 'going on' places REST above RAIN in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain someone is to check or curb them, keeping them from moving forward.

clue.text: Minister finishing early having cut a verse

indicators.note: a word that finishes early stops before its last letter, so the final letter of the minister is dropped

parts.note: a cleric is a minister of religion
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: A clergyman wraps up his sermon early after trimming a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' drops the last C of CLERIC, leaving CLERI.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a comic four-line biographical poem, a form of light verse invented by E. C. Bentley.

clue.text: Signal given by servant going round residence

indicators.note: the servant's letters go round, enclosing the residence abbreviation

parts.note: a page is a boy servant or attendant

explanation.surface: A household servant walks round the house as a sign of something to come.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foreshadow or portend, giving a warning sign of a future event.

clue.text: Hold-ups of at least 48 hours getting the Spanish trapped

indicators.note: the Spanish article is caught inside the period of time, held within it

parts.note: two or more days make at least 48 hours, so the plural days
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Travellers suffer hold-ups lasting two days or more in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Delays are setbacks that make things late, which is what hold-ups are in traffic or plans.

clue.text: Animal below mountain is a moggy without tail

indicators.note: in a down answer the rest sits below the mountain, so the mountain comes first

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain, especially in Switzerland

indicators.note: losing its tail means the final letter of the cat is cut off

parts.note: moggy is British slang for an ordinary cat

explanation.surface: Beneath a mountain a tailless cat is spotted, oddly enough an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without tail' removes the last letter of CAT, leaving CA.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American camelid grazed in the Andes for its wool, so a kind of animal.

clue.text: A sharp operator — eg Molly Malone?

explanation.surface: A shrewd dealer is compared with the fishmonger of the Dublin ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: Molly Malone, in the Irish song, wheeled her wheelbarrow through Dublin selling cockles and mussels: a seller who wheeled.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrewd, scheming businessman is a wheeler-dealer; read literally, Molly Malone was a trader who wheeled her barrow.

clue.text: Walnut bed a tad unusual? Feature of an old house

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal order, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A walnut bed is somewhat unusual, perhaps a feature of an old house.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle and daub, woven twigs plastered with mud, is a traditional building method for walls in old timber-framed houses.

clue.text: A ruddy good omen for a shepherd!

definitions.text: A ruddy good omen for a shepherd!

parts.words: A ruddy good omen for a shepherd!
parts.note: refers to the country weather saying that a reddened evening sky delights shepherds, promising fine weather next day

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a reddish evening sky is a shepherd's delight, forecasting fair weather, so it is a favourable sign.

clue.text: Old coin showing country, right?

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: A coin collector asks whether an old coin shows the right country.
explanation.definitionFit: A stater was a gold or silver coin used in ancient Greece.

clue.text: How sailor goes out to get regional prizes

parts.note: SE, the south-east, is a region, so it stands for regional here
awards are prizes

explanation.surface: A sailor heads out to collect prizes given in his region.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading seawards means moving towards the open sea, the direction a sailor takes when setting off.

clue.text: One duke accompanying a princess in the theatre

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A duke escorts a princess to the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is the title character of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Ida is the heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta of that name, a royal stage role.

clue.text: Whitener gets black to percolate out

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to leach is to drain out by liquid filtering through

explanation.surface: A whitening agent lets black dye seep away.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleach is a chemical used to whiten fabrics and remove colour.

clue.text: Gracious, a week before start of spring you'll see these birds!

parts.note: gosh and gracious are both mild exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, taken from spring

explanation.surface: An exclaiming birdwatcher says these birds appear a week before spring begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Goshawks are large hawks, so they are birds of prey.

clue.text: Sound person releasing article

indicators.note: the person lets go of the article, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a human is a person
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone lets go of a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A hum is a low continuous noise, a kind of sound.

clue.text: Bird currently by lake behind pub

indicators.note: the time and lake pieces come behind, after, the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place
now means currently
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bird is currently perched by a lake behind the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The barn owl is a pale owl that nests in farm buildings, so a bird.

clue.text: You there, learner driver — check this in your car!

parts.note: oi is an informal British shout to get someone's attention, like 'you there'
L is the plate a learner driver displays in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at a learner driver to check something in the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists routinely check the engine lubricant level with a dipstick.

clue.text: Book girl's given to bill with name inscribed

indicators.note: the name abbreviation is written inside the girl and bill pieces

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A girl's book is presented with an invoice bearing her name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' simply places AC after ALMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual reference book of calendars, tides and statistics.

clue.text: Embrocation one put on soldiers wrapped in cloth

indicators.note: the one and soldiers pieces are enclosed by the cloth

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds
I is the Roman numeral for one
men are soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: Rub-on ointment applied to wounded soldiers bandaged in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Liniment is a soothing lotion rubbed into the skin, which is what embrocation means.

clue.text: Lawyer will offer no treaty that's badly drafted

indicators.note: a badly drafted text has its words jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawyer refuses to put forward a poorly written treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage an attorney is a qualified legal practitioner, a lawyer.

clue.text: Find fault with a head, devil coming to the fore

indicators.note: the devil moves to the front, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
each means per head, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: A critic blames a leader while a devil comes forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a head' looks like a person but means 'per person', EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to accuse or challenge, calling someone's conduct into question.

clue.text: In quest for perfection, I am embracing various ladies

indicators.note: the contracted words hold the rearranged ladies inside them

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: various suggests different arrangements, so the letters of ladies are mixed

explanation.surface: Seeking perfection, a man courts several women at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' turns LADIES into DEALIS, which 'embracing' puts inside I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealism is the pursuit of high principles and perfect standards.

clue.text: Like track, one coming out from a n object in space

definitions.text: from a n object in space

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: the one leaves the track, so its letter is removed

parts.note: a trail is a track or path
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something like a track loses a piece, describing an object in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' removes I from TRAIL, leaving TRAL. The clue's 'a n' is the setter's 'an'.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral means relating to or coming from the stars.

clue.text: Move to action in place mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken out, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: in place is in site, on location

explanation.surface: Someone is spurred to act at a place that was named.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to stir up or provoke people into doing something.

clue.text: Observing zilch — not hard

indicators.note: not here means without, so the hard letter is taken away

parts.note: zilch is slang for nothing
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone watching sees absolutely nothing that is difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means observing or taking notice of something.

clue.text: President greeting character from abroad

parts.note: hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A president greets a foreign figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign character.

clue.text: Jumbly composition — it's cheap somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: A muddled artwork is dismissed as somehow cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work assembled from borrowed styles or a medley of parts.

clue.text: Motorway madness? It's an illusion

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first major motorway, with the figure 1 read as the letter I
rage is fury, a kind of madness

explanation.surface: Is road rage on the motorway just an illusion?
explanation.walkthrough: The M1, London to Leeds, is Britain's best-known motorway; its 1 doubles as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirage is an optical trick of hot air, a false image.

clue.text: Female competition changed once by statute

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A women's pageant is altered once by a new law.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty contest is a pageant in which women compete on looks.
